name: SCAMPER
description: Systematic idea generation by applying 7 transformations to an existing product/feature
steps: 1. List the current product/feature in detail. 2. For each letter (Substitute/Combine/Adapt/Modify/Put-to-other-uses/Eliminate/Reverse), ask "what if we...?" 3. Generate one idea per transformation. 4. Combine promising ideas.
output-format: Markdown list: one idea per transformation, brief rationale for each

name: Random Stimulus
description: Break linear thinking by introducing unrelated objects/words and forcing connections
steps: 1. Pick a random word from a list (or use a random object in the room). 2. Free-associate: how is this like our problem? 3. Stretch: connect it to the problem, no matter how absurd. 4. Refine absurd ideas into viable concepts.
output-format: Markdown: Stimulus word → Association → Absurd idea → Refined concept

name: Reverse Brainstorm
description: Generate ideas for the opposite problem (how to destroy/worsen/fail) then flip them
steps: 1. Restate goal as its opposite ("How to INCREASE churn instead of reduce?"). 2. Generate ideas for the bad outcome. 3. For each bad idea, write the opposite as a solution.
output-format: Two-column markdown table: Bad idea / Good idea (flip)

name: Brainwriting
description: Silent written ideation followed by sequential refinement (avoids groupthink)
steps: 1. Each person writes 3-5 initial ideas on a sheet or document. 2. Pass it to the next person who adds to or refines. 3. Rotate 3-4 rounds. 4. Synthesize the evolved ideas.
output-format: Markdown list with iteration markers showing how ideas evolved: Idea (Round 1) → Refinement (Round 2) → Final

column5: 1. 6 people, each writes 3 ideas in 5 minutes. 2. Pass to the right. 3. Next person improves or extends those 3 ideas (5 minutes). 4. Repeat 5 times. 5. Final sheet has 18 ideas, each evolved 5 times.
column6: Markdown 6x3 matrix: rows are idea streams, columns are rounds, each cell shows the idea's evolution

name: Mind Mapping
description: Radial idea structure with main idea at center and branches for sub-ideas
steps: 1. Write the core problem/goal in the center. 2. Draw branches for main themes. 3. Add sub-branches for details. 4. Use images, colors, single words per node. 5. Connect related nodes across branches.
output-format: ASCII art or text outline with indentation showing hierarchy: Core → Main branches → Sub-branches

name: Starbursting
description: Exploratory questions (Who/What/When/Where/Why/How) frame the problem space
steps: 1. Identify the subject (product/feature/problem). 2. Ask Who/What/When/Where/Why/How. 3. For each question, generate 3-5 sub-questions. 4. Ideas emerge from the answer space you've charted.
output-format: Markdown with 6 sections (one per reporter question), each containing a list of generated sub-questions and emerging ideas

name: Rolestorming
description: Adopt a persona (customer/competitor/expert/outsider) and generate ideas from their perspective
steps: 1. Choose a persona (e.g., 10-year-old user, competitor CEO, alien anthropologist, luddite). 2. Ask: what would X think about our problem? 3. Generate 5-10 ideas from that lens. 4. Repeat with 2-3 other personas.
output-format: Markdown sections by persona: [Persona name] → Ideas from this perspective (bulleted list)
